gate-is-in-process-and-cannot-fail: The TS marker writers asked Rust over the rustInvoke channel store_version_gate before every write, and the goldens record those calls (gateCalls) and, for the three cases that script a rejected channel, the warning 'bottle version gate: Rust could not be asked'. The Rust crate calls gamelib_store::version_gate in process, so there is no channel to reject and no such warning; the replay compares neither the recorded channel calls nor that one warning line. The three gate cases (reconcile-gate-rejected, record-pinned-gate-rejected, record-crossover-gate-rejected) and record-pinned-gate-answers-newer still replay: the test injects a gate that cannot be asked, or that answers newer, through the writers' Gate parameter, and the refusal (nothing written, false or null returned) is compared byte for byte.
conf-log-lines-name-the-bottle-not-its-p: The TS conf writer logged the bottle directory's full path ('Wrote cxbottle.conf (<id>) in <HOME>/Library/Application Support/CrossOver/Bottles/<name>'). The engine log never carries a profile path (T-86-15, the same rule as gamelib-info), so the Rust writer logs the directory name only. The replay compares the golden's lines with the Bottles-root prefix removed, so the id, the verb and the bottle name are still compared exactly. No file, byte or return value differs.
unreadable-marker-is-rewritten-as-the-ts: 87-11 finding 8: reconcile and recordPinnedBottleEngine overwrite a marker whose bytes are not a JSON object (the gate reports 'unreadable', which is writable), and only a marker a newer build wrote (version above 1) is never touched. The port keeps that, because the goldens (record-pinned-over-unreadable-overwritten, reconcile-marker-unreadable) record it and D-07 asks for the same bytes on disk. A marker that is unreadable is derived state with nothing recoverable in it, and the reconcile pass is what repairs it before a CrossOver probe adds a Timestamp. The round trip (roundtrip_state.rs) never rewrites an unreadable marker blindly: read returns nothing for it, so there is nothing to write back, and its bytes stay identical.
removal-refusal-names-the-bottle-not-its: The TS removeCreatedBottleDir logged 'provisionBridgeBottle: not removing partial bottle outside the Bottles root: <resolved path>' for a name that is not a single clean segment under the Bottles root. The engine log never carries a profile path (T-86-15), so the Rust function logs the quoted bottle name it was given in that place. The replay swaps the golden's path for the name of the same position in the case's names list, so the verb, the level and the order of the refusals are still compared exactly. Which names are refused, and that every directory survives, are unchanged.
removal-goes-through-the-safety-guard: The TS removeCreatedBottleDir deleted with rmSync after its own relative-path check. The Rust function checks the name the same way (a single clean segment directly under the Bottles root, so every golden refusal is the same) and then deletes through gamelib_safety remove_tree with the Bottles directory as the trust root (D-19, FND-02), which re-resolves the target and its root and refuses on a no or an unknown verdict. The goldens exercise none of the extra refusals, so the replay is byte-identical; the Rust tests add the adversarial cases the TS had no guard for (a bottle that is a symlink to a sibling bottle, a Bottles directory that cannot be resolved).
spawn-failure-text-is-the-runners-not-no: The TS goldens record a failed spawn as Node's String(error) ('Error: spawn cxbottle ENOENT'), which the create's error and log lines and the kill's warning carry. The Rust seam reports a failed spawn as the runner's stderr ('spawn <program>: <io error>'), and the create and kill functions carry that text in the same places. The replay scripts the failure with the golden's Node text so every line is still compared exactly; only the wording of a real spawn failure differs from released builds, and no behaviour or return value does.
